title: Laplace uses AI agents to stress-test robots before deployment
friendlyTitle: Laplace uses AI to find robot problems before real-world use
summary: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence is building automated red-teaming for robots, autonomous vehicles and other physical AI. Its agents use interactive simulation to search for failure cases before a system is placed in the real world.
friendlySummary: Laplace runs simulated tests that try to make robots and self-driving systems fail. This can reveal unusual problems before deployment.
whyItMatters: Physical AI failures can damage equipment or harm people, so testing only expected scenarios is insufficient. Automated adversarial simulation can broaden coverage, but it should support—not replace—real-world validation, safety cases and human accountability.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Finding failures in a simulation is safer and cheaper than finding them around people. Real-world safety checks are still necessary.
